description: CALL THIS WHEN YOU FINISH (or stop) a reverse-engineering job, even with partial results. Merges your findings into the record: summary and status replace (status only moves forward), interfaces merge by transport+name (yours replace), projects by url, install routes by method+guide, identifiers and aliases are unioned, verification is appended. The result is validated against the schema; nothing is written on error. Link to your protocol docs/code hosted elsewhere; never include firmware images, vendor code, keys, or anything defeating Remote ID, geofencing or other safety functions (POLICY.md). Set provenance.ai_assisted honestly. Then open a pull request — the result gives the commands.

allow_downgrade.description: Allow lowering the status (only when the previous status was wrong; explain why in summary or verification notes).

patch.description: Findings to merge into the record.

identifiers.description: Identifiers to add (unioned with the existing ones).

install.description: Ways to install the open firmware or software, linking to the project's own guide (nothing is hosted here); merged by method+guide (yours replace).

difficulty.description: easy = no tools, device stays closed; medium = cable or command line; hard = opening, soldering, programmer.

firmware_constraints.description: e.g. "stock firmware after 2.x is patched: does not work".

guide.description: URL of the project's official step-by-step guide.

installer.description: URL of the official installer tool, when one exists.

method.description: web-serial = browser installer, ota-exploit (e.g. cloudcutter), vendor-upload (stock web UI accepts the image), usb-bootloader (fastboot/DFU), sd-card, serial (UART, device opened), spi-programmer, pairing (no flashing), host-software.

project.description: Name of the project (in `projects`) this route installs.

tools.description: What to have, e.g. ["USB-serial adapter, 3.3 V"].

interfaces.description: Interfaces you documented; one with the same transport+name replaces the existing one.

confidence.description: How sure you are; AI-derived, untested work is low or medium.

spec.description: URL of the protocol description you wrote (repo, gist, wiki).

projects.description: Your code or docs (open license, hosted elsewhere); merged by url.

ai_assisted.description: true if an AI agent did any of the work (always say so).

status.description: New status; it can only move forward (unknown → in-progress → partial-protocol → controllable → open-firmware).

summary.description: One plain-text paragraph: what the device is and what is now known. Replaces the current summary.

vendor_support.description: State of the vendor's own service.

method.description: hardware-replay = replayable test run on a real device; this is what earns the verified badge.

release_claim_of.description: Remove the live claims of this claimant (the `who` you used in claim_device) now that the work is published.

name: publish_findings
title: Publish what you found
